import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 224

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/224](https://www.erdosproblems.com/224)
- [DaGr62] Danzer, L. and Gr\"{u}nbaum, B., *\"{U}ber zwei Probleme
  bez\"{u}glich konvexer K\"{o}rper von P. Erd\H{o}s und von V. L. Klee*.
  Math. Z. (1962), 95-99.
-/

namespace Erdos224

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/-- The angle $yxz$ is obtuse. -/
def ObtuseAt {d : ℕ} (x y z : ℝ^d) : Prop :=
  inner ℝ (y - x) (z - x) < 0

/--
If $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is any set of $2^d+1$ points then some three points in $A$ determine an obtuse angle.

The general case was proved by Danzer and Gr\"{u}nbaum [DaGr62].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos224.lean"]
theorem erdos_224 {d : ℕ} (A : Finset (ℝ^d)) (hcard : A.card = 2 ^ d + 1) :
    ∃ x y z : ℝ^d, x ∈ A ∧ y ∈ A ∧ z ∈ A ∧
      x ≠ y ∧ x ≠ z ∧ y ≠ z ∧ ObtuseAt x y z := by
  sorry

end Erdos224

reformulations.difference: Uses a negative inner product instead of an explicit geometric angle greater than π/2.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved `ObtuseAt x y z ↔ Real.pi / 2 < EuclideanGeometry.angle y x z` in scratch. For nonzero displacement vectors, their positive norm product makes the inner-product sign agree with the cosine sign. Repeated-point cases satisfy neither side. Including straight angles is faithful: Danzer–Grünbaum's introduction poses the complementary condition that every angle is at most a right angle, not a restriction to nondegenerate triangles.

reformulations.difference: The original paper gives an upper bound of 2^d for non-obtuse point sets; Lean uses the equivalent 2^d+1-point existence formulation stated on the problem website.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A non-obtuse set exceeding 2^d points has a subset of exactly 2^d+1 points, contradicting the existence assertion. Conversely, a 2^d+1-point set without the required triple contradicts the upper bound. Negative inner product already forces all three points to be distinct. This equivalence was proved as `Review224.threshold_iff_nonobtuse_bound` without using the reviewed theorem.

sources_consulted: Danzer, L. and Grünbaum, B., Über zwei Probleme bezüglich konvexer Körper von P. Erdös und von V. L. Klee, Math. Z. 79 (1962), 95–99, DOI 10.1007/BF01193107. Full paper read through GDZ OCR: https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/gdzocr/PPN266833020_0079/00000105.xml through 00000109.xml.
Crossref bibliographic metadata for DOI 10.1007/BF01193107, retrieved by title query at https://api.crossref.org/works
review.notes: Both declarations are faithful. The website records PROVED (LEAN), matching the metadata. Dimension zero is harmless: ℝ^0 is a singleton, so the required cardinality 2 is impossible. Lean tests covered repeated points, acute/right/straight angles, and a realizable three-point set in dimension one. The cited v4.29.1 proof checked against the sandbox's v4.33.1 after three scratch-only compatibility edits; a bridge to the exact repository statement depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, extra-tests.lean, and cited-proof-bridge.lean.
